title: Tradeoff matrix: quantization, model variants, and rollout gates (draft)
content:
Purpose

Working draft to collect a pragmatic tradeoff matrix and suggested evaluation gates that let us safely enable cheaper serving configurations (quantization, smaller model variant, aggressive batching, reduced context) while limiting user-visible quality regressions. This is intended for product + applied-ml + serving runtime to use when creating rollout policies for Redwood Optimize suggestions and automated fallback rules.

Background / motivation

We get repeated requests to recommend lower-cost serving configs for customers (esp. high-volume embedding and generation workloads). Customers prefer lower cost but product teams require guardrails to keep quality regressions minimal. Previously we had ad-hoc checks (manual A/B tests, spot human eval). We need a repeatable checklist + numeric gate thresholds that map to outcomes in our cost spreadsheet scenarios.

Definitions / sample cheaper configs considered

- q8_0: 8-bit quantization (no KF cache changes). Lowered compute cost ~25-35% on typical GPUs.
- q4_1: 4-bit quantization (symmetric asymmetric choices). Lower cost ~40-55% but more brittle on some layers.
- small-variant: next-smaller model family (e.g., 13B -> 7B) with same tokenizer. Cost reduction ~50-70% depending on latency SLO.
- short-context: 50% max_seq_len cap (trim long contexts at runtime). Useful for chat backends.
- batch-heavy: increase batching window / higher tail p99 but lower per-token cost.
- hybrid-fallback: route to cheaper config with automatic fallback to baseline on confidence/hallucination triggers.

Core objectives for gates

- Minimize user-visible helpfulness regression: target delta helpfulness <= 2 percentage points (absolute) on primary eval set used by the customer.
- Limit hallucination increase: delta hallucination <= 0.5 percentage points (absolute) measured by our hallucination classifier and spot human eval.
- Preserve latency percentiles: p95 latency must not exceed baseline p95 by more than 20% for latency-sensitive routes (config-level SLO enforcement).
- Cost delta: prefer configs that provide >=20% cost reduction for any gating to justify rollout overhead.
- Operational safety: memory OOM risk must be <0.1% during stress runs.

Tradeoff matrix (how to use)

For each customer workload or internal benchmark:
1) Run deterministic eval harness (same prompts, same random seeds) against baseline + each candidate cheaper config. Collect: token cost estimate, helpfulness score, hallucination rate, p50/p95 latency, OOMs, and delta in output length.
2) Populate the cost spreadsheet (linked above) with scenario assumptions (QPS, average prompt length, session recency).
3) Accept configuration if all hard gates pass. If helpfulness delta is marginal (2-3 pp), tag for "canary with metric-level mitigation" instead of full rollout.

Suggested numeric gates (initial, conservative)

- Helpful score: baseline helpfulness = H_b. Accept if H_new >= H_b - 2.0 (absolute).
- Hallucination: baseline hall = S_b. Accept if S_new <= S_b + 0.5.
- ROUGE/f1-like automated metrics: only allow drop <= 3% relative if helpfulness still within gate.
- Latency: p95_new <= p95_b * 1.20 for routes with latency SLO tag. For background batch jobs, p95 allowance up to 1.5x.
- Cost reduction: min 20% lower per-token or per-request cost.
- Stability: no more than 1 out of 1000 requests triggers an OOM or catastrophic decoder failure in stress tests.

Evaluation harness notes

- Always run both automatic metrics (our eval pipeline) and a small human panel (n=40 blind pairwise) for any config that passes automatic gates. Human eval should target the exact customer prompt distribution where possible.
- Use paired comparisons vs baseline on the same seed list to control variance. Report bootstrap CI for any helpfulness delta.
- If helpfulness delta CI overlaps 0 and median delta < 2.0, prefer canary rollout.

Rollout patterns and mitigations

- Canary-by-user: enable cheaper config for 1% of users, compare business metrics and eval probes for 7 days, automatically revert if any metric crosses threshold.
- Canary-by-route: enable for low-risk routes (summarization, code-completion with high hallucination tolerance) first.
- Confidence-based fallback: models tagged with a confidence predictor; route responses below threshold to baseline model synchronously or asynchronously re-score.
- Dynamic hybrid: prefer cheaper config; if hallucination classifier triggers, stream a graceful degrade message and re-request the baseline in the background if latency budget allows.

Spreadsheet columns to add (practical)

- scenario_id
- workload_description (prompts per user, average tokens in/out)
- baseline_model_tag
- candidate_config (q8_0, q4_1, small-variant, etc.)
- per_token_cost_estimate_usd
- delta_cost_pct
- helpfulness_baseline, helpfulness_candidate, delta_help_abs, delta_help_CI_low, delta_help_CI_high
- hallucination_baseline, hallucination_candidate, delta_hall_abs
- latency_p95_baseline_ms, latency_p95_candidate_ms
- ooms_in_stress_runs, fail_rate_pct
- recommended_action (block | canary | rollout | opt-in)

Open questions / risk areas

- Our automated hallucination detector's calibration across quantized configs is not validated; potential measurement bias. Need to add mixing of quantized outputs into detector retraining. (JIRA-OPT-931).
- Some customer prompt distributions are adversarial to q4 quantization (rare tokens in long tails). We should capture token coverage diagnostics in the harness.
- Interaction effects: short-context + q4 is notably worse for multi-turn retrieval augmented prompts. We should run combinatorial stress tests.

Next steps (short runway)

- Product + applied-ml to pick 4 representative customer workload demos by Jan 24.
- Eng-serving-runtime to produce automated CI job that runs stress evals for candidate configs nightly and writes to the linked sheet (owner: Mateo Ruiz).
- Draft a lightweight runbook for canary rollback triggers and add to Console rollouts docs.
- Schedule a 2-week canary with partner customer for q8 on summarization route (owner: Priya Sharma).

Notes to self / TODOs

- Add example paired-human-eval rubric to the sheet.
- Verify cost accounting assumptions used by infra (are we including preemption overhead on spot?)
- Align with SRE on p95 measurement method (wall-clock vs internal queue time).

References

- internal cost scenarios sheet (linked), prior playbook drafts: CONFLUENCE-OPTIMIZE-PLAYBOOK-V2
- Github PR with quantization profiles: /model-configs PR #218

If this doc looks reasonable, I'll convert to a short playbook checklist and propose a default gate set for "low-risk" vs "high-risk" routes.

-- Sofia
